statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-46598 (GO-2026-5033, GHSA-9m57-25v3-79x9): in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent, crafted input can produce a malformed ed25519.PrivateKey that panics when used. The advisory lists ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent and the internal parseEd25519Key and parseEd25519Cert in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent, and it is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto 0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5033, https://go.dev/issue/79596, https://go.dev/cl/781360, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The build information of the frontend program lists golang.org/x/crypto (v0.45.0 through v0.59.0 across the builds) and the program links the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package, but no function table contains a golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent function, so none of the four listed functions is present in any build. As a positive control, the same reader lists all four functions in a linux/amd64 test program built with golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 that calls agent.ServeAgent and agent.ForwardToAgent. The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the golang.org/x/crypto version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

CVE-2026-46598 (GO-2026-5033, GHSA-9m57-25v3-79x9): for certain crafted inputs golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent built an ed25519.PrivateKey by casting malformed wire bytes, which panicked when the key was used. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5033, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9m57-25v3-79x9, https://go.dev/issue/79596, https://go.dev/cl/781360, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. The Go vulnerability database names the vulnerable code as the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent functions ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseEd25519Cert and parseEd25519Key. This package does not contain that code. We read the Go build information and the function table (pclntab) of /usr/bin/external-dns, the single file each package installs (a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0), in every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, 33 builds, each for x86_64 and aarch64), each checked against its index checksum. The function table of every build contains runtime.main, which confirms the listing works on that file. The build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.45.0 in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.20.0-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.20.0-r4 to 0.21.0-r1, v0.50.0 in 0.21.0-r2 to 0.21.0-r3, v0.51.0 in 0.21.0-r4, and v0.52.0 or later from 0.21.0-r5 (v0.58.0 in the current 0.24.0-r5), but no build's function table contains any function of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package or of golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent. The only name under golang.org/x/crypto/ssh in any build's function table is golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal.init, the initializer of the separate ssh/terminal package, in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13. A raw byte search of every build also finds no "golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent.", ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseEd25519Cert or parseEd25519Key. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search find ssh/agent.ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseEd25519Cert and parseEd25519Key in a test program we built with golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0 (the last release before the fix) for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

CVE-2026-46598 (GO-2026-5033, GHSA-9m57-25v3-79x9): golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent built an ed25519 private key by casting malformed wire bytes, so certain crafted key or certificate data sent to an agent could make it panic. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by CL 781360, which changes ssh/agent/server.go (parseEd25519Key and parseEd25519Cert): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5033, https://go.dev/issue/79596, https://go.dev/cl/781360, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI. The Go vulnerability database lists ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseEd25519Cert and parseEd25519Key in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent as the vulnerable functions. We read every published node-exporter-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 27 versions, 1.10.2-r0 to 1.13.1-r0, each matching its repository index checksum. We also read, on both architectures, every published package built from the node-exporter and node-exporter-fips sources: node-exporter and node-exporter-dev in the DHI Alpine repository, and node-exporter-fips and node-exporter-fips-dev in the DHI Alpine security repository, 216 packages in all, 27 versions of each. Each of these packages holds exactly one file, /usr/bin/node_exporter, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. Their Go build information lists the golang.org/x/crypto module (v0.45.0 in 1.10.2-r0 to 1.10.2-r3, v0.49.0 in 1.11.0-r0 to 1.11.1-r3, then v0.52.0 to v0.58.0 from 1.11.1-r4), but none of the 216 programs links golang.org/x/crypto/ssh or golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent: a Go function-table (pclntab) reader finds no function under golang.org/x/crypto/ssh in any of them, and a byte search of every program, which also catches inlined function names, finds no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh name. The only golang.org/x/crypto packages in the function tables are bcrypt, blowfish and pbkdf2, and the reader finds runtime.main in every program. As a positive control, the same reader lists golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent.ForwardToAgent, ServeAgent, parseEd25519Key and parseEd25519Cert in test programs we built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (CGO_ENABLED=0, -ldflags=-w, with and without inlining) against the vulnerable golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 that serve and forward an agent, and the byte search finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent names in every control build. None of the advisory's vulnerable functions is present in any published build.

It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 by CL 781360, which changes ssh/agent/server.go (parseEd25519Key and parseEd25519Cert): https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5033, https://go.dev/issue/79596, https://go.dev/cl/781360, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/a082jnz-LvI.
